name: Build Muscle Plant-based, Whole Foods
summary: Tikka-style masala, gado-gado, a Moroccan-style tempeh and lupini stew and maple baked white beans, in a week that gets about a quarter of its calories from protein, all from food, with no powders and no seitan. Carbs stay whole-food: potatoes, oats, quinoa, buckwheat and fruit.
howItWorks:
**Built for training days.** About a quarter of each day's calories come from protein, all from food, with no powders and no seitan. That is enough for most people building muscle at these calories. The carbs are potatoes, oats, quinoa, buckwheat and fruit. Calorie levels from 2,200 to 2,800 scale the portions a little. There is no bigger size, because iron gets too close to its upper limit.

**Soy and lupini share the protein.** Tofu, tempeh, edamame and fortified soy drink work alongside lupini beans, lentils, chickpeas, beans, peanuts and seeds. Lupini come ready to eat in jars at Italian, Portuguese and Middle Eastern grocers and some large supermarkets. No lupini? Use white beans or chickpeas; those days have less protein. If you take thyroid medicine, mention the soy to your care provider.

**Fibre, beans and allergens.** This is a very high-fibre week. If you don't usually eat many beans, ease in over a week or two with smaller servings of the lupini and beans, drink plenty of water and rinse all canned beans. It contains soy, peanut, walnuts, mustard and lupin. Lupin is related to peanut, so people with a peanut allergy can react to it too.

**B12, iodine and supplements.** Fortified soy drink goes into every breakfast for B12 and calcium (check the carton). Food already brings plenty of calcium and iron, so choose a B12-only supplement and skip extra calcium or iron unless your care provider says otherwise. If you're over 50, check this week with them first. Iodine and vitamin D are low here, so use iodized salt and ask them about both.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday to Saturday dinners make two portions, so the next day's lunch is done. Saturday's maple baked white beans are the weekend project and freeze well. Sunday's koshari-style bowl is a single portion. Cool leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming. Use sealed packs of silken tofu, and use an opened pack within 2 days.

proteinFloor.why: From whole foods without seitan or powders, 30% of calories as protein needs far more soy than studies have looked at; 25% is still about 140 to 175 g of protein a day at these calories, plenty for building muscle.

recipes.name: Cardamom apple oatmeal with silken tofu, hemp and peanut butter
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by cardamom-spiced porridges from Scandinavia and India
recipes.about: Rolled oats simmered in fortified soy drink, with silken tofu melted in until the bowl is creamy and an apple softened with cardamom and cinnamon on top. A spoonful of peanut butter and hemp hearts finish it. It is a **big, warming bowl of protein**, with about a cup of fortified soy drink in it, before the day starts.
steps: Rinse the apple, then dice it, skin on. Mash the silken tofu with a fork until it looks like loose ricotta.
Bring the soy drink to a gentle simmer in a small pot. Stir in the oats, ground flax, cinnamon and salt and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the mashed silken tofu, a little at a time, until the oatmeal is smooth and glossy.
In a small pan over medium heat, warm the apple with the cardamom and maple syrup for 3 to 4 minutes, until it just softens and smells sweet.
Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl, top with the warm apple, and finish with the peanut butter and the hemp hearts.
recipes.tip: Cook a double batch of plain oatmeal on Sunday, cool it in a shallow container within 1 hour and keep it covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat a portion with a splash of soy drink until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and stir the tofu in fresh. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Chocolate banana oatmeal with silken tofu cream and peanut butter
recipes.about: Hot oats under a spoonful of chocolate cream blended from silken tofu, banana, cocoa and maple syrup, finished with peanut butter and hemp hearts. It tastes like dessert for breakfast, and the tofu cream quietly carries **a good part of the protein**. Fortified soy drink cooks into the oats.
steps: Peel the banana. Blend three quarters of it with the silken tofu, cocoa, maple syrup and a splash of the soy drink for 30 seconds, until completely smooth. This is the chocolate cream.
Bring the rest of the soy drink to a gentle simmer in a small pot. Stir in the oats, ground flax, cinnamon and salt and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Spoon the oatmeal into a bowl. Slice the remaining banana over it and add the chocolate cream.
Finish with a spoonful of peanut butter and the hemp hearts.
recipes.tip: Make the chocolate cream the night before; it keeps up to 2 days covered in the fridge. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Aloo tofu bhurji with lentils and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian egg bhurji, with tofu in the egg's place
recipes.about: Crumbled extra-firm tofu and green lentils cooked the way Indian kitchens scramble eggs, with onion, tomato, ginger, cumin and chili, piled over golden potatoes and wilted spinach. It is a savoury, **protein-heavy breakfast** that holds you for hours. A glass of fortified soy drink goes alongside.

ingredients.note: canned green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
a glass of fortified soy drink on the side

steps: Rinse the potato, tomato, spinach, carrot, cilantro and lentils. Cut the potato into small cubes so it cooks quickly. Drain the tofu, pat it dry and crumble it with your hands into small pieces.

Warm half the oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the potato with a pinch of the salt, cover, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and tender. Tip onto a plate.
In the same pan, warm the rest of the oil and toast the cumin seeds for 20 seconds, until they sizzle and smell nutty. Add the onion, carrot, ginger and garlic and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.

Stir in the tomato, turmeric and chili powder and cook for 3 minutes, until the tomato breaks down. Add the crumbled tofu, the lentils and the rest of the salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring and mashing a few lentils, until hot and dry at the edges.
Fold in the spinach until it wilts, then the garam masala and lemon juice. Serve over the potatoes with the cilantro and hemp hearts, and a glass of cold soy drink.
recipes.tip: Cube and boil the potatoes the night before, cool and refrigerate them within 1 hour, and they crisp in 6 minutes; use them within 3 days. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Savoury buckwheat bowl with lentils, crisp tempeh, mushrooms and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha with mushrooms
recipes.about: A warm breakfast bowl of toasty buckwheat with green lentils, golden tempeh, browned mushrooms, wilted spinach and creamy avocado, seasoned with garlic, soy sauce and lemon. It is **savoury, crunchy and very high in protein**, with a glass of fortified soy drink on the side.

ingredients.note: canned green or brown lentils, rinsed and drained
a glass of fortified soy drink on the side

steps: Rinse the mushrooms, spinach, avocado and lentils. Rinse the buckwheat in a sieve and toast it in a dry pot over medium heat for 2 minutes. Add twice its volume of water, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, then rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Steam the tempeh cubes over simmering water for 8 minutes, then pat dry. Brown them in half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until crisp. Tip onto a plate.

In the same pan, cook the mushrooms in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes, until browned. Add the garlic and soy sauce for 1 minute, then the lentils and spinach until the spinach wilts and the lentils are hot.

Spoon the buckwheat into a bowl, top with the mushrooms, lentils and spinach, the crisp tempeh and sliced avocado, and finish with the lemon juice, pepper, chopped walnuts and hemp hearts. Serve with a glass of cold soy drink.
recipes.tip: Cook a batch of buckwheat on Sunday, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep it up to 3 days and reheat it until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).

recipes.name: Taco-spiced lentil and tofu bowl with crispy potatoes and lime slaw
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mexican tacos de papa and taco bowls
recipes.about: Crispy potato cubes under green lentils, black beans and crumbled tofu cooked with chili, cumin and smoked paprika, with a crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw, avocado and a spoonful of lime tofu crema. It is a Tex-Mex style lunch bowl that is **easy to build and very filling**.

ingredients.note: canned green or brown lentils, rinsed
blended with the lime into a crema

steps: Rinse the potato, cabbage, carrot, cilantro and avocado. Cut the potato into small cubes, skin on. Toss the shredded cabbage and grated carrot with half the lime juice, a pinch of the salt and half the cilantro, and blend the silken tofu with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt for the crema.

Microwave the potato cubes in a covered bowl with a splash of water for 4 minutes, until just tender, and drain. Warm half the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and fry them for 8 to 10 minutes, turning now and then, until golden and crisp at the edges. Tip into a bowl.

Warm the rest of the oil in the same pan over medium heat. Add the crumbled tofu, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano and tomato paste and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the tofu is dry and deep red-orange.
Add the rinsed lentils and black beans and a splash of water and warm for 3 minutes, mashing a few of the beans so the filling holds together. Season with the rest of the salt.
Spoon the filling over the crispy potatoes and top with the slaw, lime crema, sliced avocado, pumpkin seeds and the rest of the cilantro.
recipes.tip: Microwave the potato cubes the night before, cool and refrigerate them within 1 hour, and they crisp in 5 minutes; use them within 3 days. Rinse canned lentils and beans well; it helps with gas. Keep opened tins covered in the fridge and use them within 2 days. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Greek-style white beans and potatoes in tomato with lemon-oregano tofu "feta" and lupini
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek gigantes plaki and marinated feta
recipes.about: White beans, potatoes and carrots simmered in a garlicky tomato and oregano sauce with spinach folded in, topped with crumbled tofu that has soaked up lemon, oregano and garlic, and a little dish of oiled lupini on the side like a Greek taverna meze. It tastes like a baked Greek bean dish, and the beans, tofu and lupini give it **a big serving of protein**.

ingredients.note: jarred ready-to-eat lupini, soaked and rinsed

steps: Soak the lupini in fresh cold water in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, since the jar brine is very salty. Press the tofu between clean towels for 10 minutes, then cut it into small cubes. Toss it with half the lemon juice, half the oregano and a third of the garlic, and refrigerate it for at least 20 minutes while the sauce cooks. Never reuse the marinade.

Rinse the spinach and potato. Warm half the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the rest of the garlic and the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.

Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the potato cubes, the rest of the oregano, the salt and a splash of water. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the rinsed white beans and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick. Fold in the spinach until it wilts.

Season with the rest of the lemon juice and the pepper. Drain and rinse the lupini, taste one and soak a little longer if it is still salty, then toss them with the rest of the oil and a pinch of pepper. Spoon the stew into bowls, drain the tofu from its marinade, throw the marinade away and crumble the tofu over the top. Serve the lupini alongside. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and take it to work in a cold bag with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: To freeze the stew, leave the tofu and lupini off. Cool it within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days. Never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Keep opened tins of beans covered in the fridge and use them within 2 days. Lupini are related to peanuts, so skip them if you have a peanut or lupin allergy. Eat only jarred or canned ready-to-eat lupini, never dry or raw lupin beans, and throw out any bean that tastes bitter. No lupini? Add a few more white beans to the stew instead. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Georgian-style kidney bean lobio with crisp tempeh and walnuts over buckwheat
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Georgian lobio and its walnut and coriander flavours
recipes.about: A thick, herby bean stew in the spirit of Georgian lobio, made with kidney beans, mushrooms, ground walnuts, coriander and lemon, topped with crisp tempeh and spooned over toasty buckwheat. It is **rich, savoury and very high in protein**, and tastes better the second day.
steps: Rinse the cilantro, mushrooms and buckwheat. Toast the buckwheat in a dry pot over medium heat for 2 minutes, add twice its volume of water and a pinch of the salt, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until the water is gone. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Steam the tempeh cubes over simmering water for 8 minutes, then pat dry. Brown them in half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, until crisp. Tip onto a plate.

In the same pan, warm the rest of the oil and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until they release their water and brown. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft and golden, then the garlic, coriander, paprika, cumin and tomato paste for 2 minutes.

Add the rinsed kidney beans, the walnuts and enough water to just cover. Simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few of the beans against the pan, until the stew is thick and the walnuts have melted into it.

Stir in the lemon juice, half the cilantro, the pepper and the rest of the salt. Serve over the buckwheat topped with the crisp tempeh and the rest of the cilantro. Cool the second portion with its buckwheat in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and take it to work in a cold bag with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: Buckwheat groats are gluten-free by nature. Buy ones marked certified if you avoid gluten. Keep an opened tin of beans covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Gado-gado plate with tofu, tempeh, potatoes and peanut sauce
recipes.about: A big Indonesian-style plate of seared tofu and tempeh, warm potatoes, edamame, steamed cabbage and carrot and fresh cucumber, all spooned over with a lime, ginger and peanut sauce and scattered with chopped roasted peanuts. It is **filling, colourful and full of protein**, and the sauce keeps in a jar.
steps: Rinse the potato, cabbage, carrot and cucumber. Boil the potato cubes in plenty of water for 10 to 12 minutes, until tender, adding the cabbage, carrot and frozen edamame for the last 3 minutes, until the edamame is steaming hot all the way through. Drain well.
Steam the tempeh slices over simmering water for 8 minutes, then pat dry. Pat the tofu dry.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu and tempeh for 7 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides.

Crush half the chopped peanuts finely, then whisk them with the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, ginger, garlic and chili powder and 1 to 2 tablespoons of warm water into a thick, pourable sauce.

Arrange the potatoes, edamame, vegetables, cucumber, tofu and tempeh on plates, spoon the rich peanut sauce over the top and scatter with the rest of the peanuts. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and take it to work in a cold bag with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: Keep the sauce in a jar and pack the cucumber separately, and add both cold after reheating, so the vegetables stay bright. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Tofu, lentil and chickpea tikka-style masala with quinoa
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian tikka masala, made with tofu, lentils and chickpeas
recipes.about: Seared tofu and chickpeas in a rich, mildly spiced tomato sauce thickened with red lentils and made creamy with silken tofu, with garam masala, ginger and a squeeze of lemon, spooned over quinoa. It has **all the comfort of a takeout masala** and a big hit of protein.
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and simmer it in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes. Cover off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff. Rinse the red lentils and the cilantro.
Pat the tofu dry. Warm a third of the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu cubes for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden. Tip onto a plate.

Lower the heat, add the rest of the oil and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric and chili powder and cook for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.

Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the red lentils, the salt and a cup (250 mL) of water and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are completely soft and the sauce is thick. Let the sauce cool for 5 minutes, then blend it with the silken tofu, venting the lid, until smooth and silky. Return it to the pan.
Add the rinsed chickpeas and the seared tofu and warm gently for 5 minutes. Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice, and scatter with the cilantro.

Serve over the quinoa. Cool the second portion with its quinoa in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and take it to work in a cold bag with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: To freeze it, cool the masala within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days. Never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Keep an opened tin of chickpeas covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Moroccan-style tempeh, chickpea and lupini stew with sweet potato, carrot and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Moroccan tagines and their sweet-savoury spicing
recipes.about: Crisp tempeh, chickpeas and tender lupini simmered with sweet potato and carrot in a tomato sauce scented with ras el hanout, cinnamon, ginger and lemon, with spinach folded in at the end. It is **sweet, warming and rich in protein**, and even better the next day.

ingredients.note: jarred ready-to-eat lupini, soaked and rinsed

steps: Rinse the spinach, carrot, sweet potato and cilantro. Drain the lupini, cover them with fresh cold water and soak them in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, since the jar brine is very salty. Drain, rinse and taste one, and soak a little longer if it still tastes salty. Steam the tempeh cubes over simmering water for 8 minutes, then pat dry.
Warm half the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown the tempeh for 6 minutes, until crisp at the edges. Tip onto a plate.
Lower the heat, add the rest of the oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, ras el hanout, cinnamon and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the sweet potato, the carrot, the salt and enough water to come halfway up the vegetables. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the rinsed chickpeas and the lupini and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Fold in the spinach until it wilts, then the lemon juice and the tempeh.

Scatter with the cilantro. Cool the second portion in a shallow container within 1 hour and refrigerate it. It keeps up to 3 days; reheat it once until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F), and take it to work in a cold bag with an ice pack.
recipes.tip: To freeze it, leave the tempeh off. Cool the stew within 1 hour, freeze up to 2 months, thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days. Never refreeze, and reheat to 74 °C (165 °F). Crisp the tempeh fresh. Keep an opened tin of chickpeas covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Lupini are related to peanuts, so skip them if you have a peanut or lupin allergy. Eat only jarred or canned ready-to-eat lupini, never dry or raw lupin beans, and throw out any bean that tastes bitter. No lupini? Use more chickpeas instead.

recipes.name: Maple baked white beans with smoky tempeh, sweet potato wedges and wilted spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Quebec and New England baked beans
recipes.about: White beans slow-baked in a sticky sauce of tomato, maple syrup, mustard and smoked paprika with crumbled tempeh, served with roasted sweet potato wedges and wilted spinach. It is a **cozy weekend pot with plenty of protein**, and it freezes well.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Scrub the sweet potato, cut it into wedges and toss with a third of the oil on a baking tray. Set aside.

Warm half the remaining oil in an oven-safe pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, ground yellow mustard seed (dry mustard), smoked paprika and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Crumble in the tempeh and cook for 4 minutes. Stir in the rinsed white beans, the maple syrup, the soy sauce and water to just cover.

Bring to a simmer, then cover the pot and put it in the oven. Put the sweet potato tray in at the same time. After 30 minutes, uncover the pot, turn the wedges, and bake 10 minutes more, until the sauce is thick and glossy and the wedges are browned.
Rinse the spinach and wilt it in a pan with the rest of the oil and a pinch of pepper for 2 minutes. Stir the lemon juice into the beans.

Serve the beans with the sweet potato wedges and spinach. Cool the second portion within 1 hour, then refrigerate it for tomorrow or freeze it up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge and use within 2 days. Never refreeze, and reheat until steaming hot, 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: Keep opened tins of beans covered in the fridge and use them within 2 days. A slow cooker works too with canned beans: 6 hours on low, with the wedges roasted separately.

recipes.name: Koshari-style bowl with buckwheat, red lentils, chickpeas and seared tofu
recipes.about: Buckwheat, red lentils and chickpeas piled under a spiced tomato sauce with seared tofu and crisp fried onions, in the spirit of Egyptian koshari. It is a **hearty, tangy single-bowl dinner** with garlic and lemon to lift it.
steps: Rinse the lentils and the buckwheat. Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 8 to 10 minutes, until just tender, and drain. Toast the buckwheat in a dry pot for 2 minutes, add twice its volume of water, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, then rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, spread half the onion on a lined tray with half the oil and a pinch of salt, and roast at 200 °C (400 °F) for 15 minutes, stirring once, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.

In a small saucepan, soften the rest of the onion with a splash of water for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin, chili powder and tomato paste for 1 minute. Add the crushed tomatoes and the salt and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick.
Pat the tofu dry and sear the cubes in the rest of the oil in a small non-stick pan for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden.
Stir the lemon juice into the sauce. Pile the buckwheat, lentils and rinsed chickpeas in a bowl, spoon the sauce over, and top with the tofu, the crisp onions and the cilantro.
recipes.tip: Keep an opened tin of chickpeas covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Lemon-garlic edamame
recipes.about: Warm shelled edamame tossed with garlic, lemon and chili. A **simple, high-protein soy snack** that takes five minutes.
steps: Cook the frozen edamame in boiling water for 4 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through, then drain well.
Toss with the oil, garlic, chili, salt and lemon juice while still warm. Eat warm or chilled.
recipes.tip: Cook a double batch and keep half covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Ginger-soy baked tofu strips with apple
recipes.about: Extra-firm tofu strips baked in a sticky glaze of soy sauce, fresh ginger, lime and a touch of maple until chewy and caramelized, with a crisp apple on the side. It is a **meaty, high-protein snack** that eats well hot or cold.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Press the tofu between clean towels for 10 minutes, then cut it into strips.
Whisk the soy sauce, ginger, lime juice, maple syrup, oil and garlic with a tablespoon of water. Toss the tofu in half of it and spread on a lined tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, brush with the rest of the glaze, and bake for 10 minutes more, until sticky and browned at the edges.
Rinse and slice the apple and serve it alongside. Keep leftover strips refrigerated for up to 3 days. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Bake a double tray on Sunday and keep it in the fridge for the first 3 days.

recipes.name: Raspberry-ginger smoothie with silken tofu and soy drink
recipes.about: Frozen raspberries, banana, fresh ginger, silken tofu, peanut butter and fortified soy drink blended into a thick, cold smoothie you can drink with a straw or eat with a spoon. Hemp hearts and ground flax add plant omega-3. A **cold, filling snack**.
steps: Put the soy drink, silken tofu, peanut butter, frozen raspberries, banana, ginger, lime juice and cinnamon in a blender and blend for 45 seconds, until completely smooth.
Add the hemp hearts and ground flax and pulse twice. Pour into a tall glass, adding a splash more soy drink if you want it thinner, and enjoy right away.
recipes.tip: Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Smoky paprika peanut, pumpkin seed and hemp mix
recipes.about: Roasted peanuts, pumpkin seeds, walnuts and hemp hearts toasted with smoked paprika, a little maple syrup and salt until crisp and glossy. A **pocket-size, crunchy snack** you make once and scoop all week.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Toss the peanuts, pumpkin seeds, walnuts and hemp hearts with the maple syrup, smoked paprika and salt on a lined tray.
Toast for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once, until fragrant and glossy. Cool completely; the mix crisps up as it cools.
Portion into a small jar or bag. It keeps for 2 weeks in a sealed container at room temperature.
recipes.tip: Make a big jar on Sunday and scoop a portion each day.

recipes.name: Smoky paprika lupini beans with cucumber and carrot
recipes.about: Tender jarred lupini beans tossed with lemon, garlic, smoked paprika and cilantro, with cool cucumber and carrot on the side. It is a Mediterranean-style snack that is **very high in protein**, and nothing needs cooking.

ingredients.note: jarred ready-to-eat lupini, soaked and rinsed

steps: Drain the lupini, cover them with fresh cold water and soak them in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, since the jar brine is very salty. Drain, rinse and taste one, and soak a little longer if it still tastes salty.
Rinse the cilantro, cucumber and carrot. Toss the lupini with the lemon juice, garlic, oil, cilantro, smoked paprika and salt.

Serve with the cucumber and carrot. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Lupini are related to peanuts, so skip them if you have a peanut or lupin allergy. Eat only jarred or canned ready-to-eat lupini, never dry or raw lupin beans, and throw out any bean that tastes bitter.
recipes.tip: Peel each bean by pinching the skin off with your teeth, the way they are eaten in Italy and Egypt, or eat them whole. No lupini? Use the same weight of rinsed canned white beans or chickpeas; the day will be lower in protein.

recipes.name: Lupini ceviche-style salad with tomato, lime, avocado and cilantro
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Peruvian ceviche and Mexican pico de gallo, made with lupini beans
recipes.about: Ready-to-eat lupini beans tossed with ripe tomato, a little onion, cilantro, lime and oil, with creamy avocado and hemp hearts for crunch. A **fresh snack that is mostly protein**, with no cooking at all.

ingredients.note: jarred ready-to-eat lupini, soaked and rinsed

steps: Drain the lupini, cover them with fresh cold water and soak them in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, since the jar brine is very salty. Drain, rinse and taste one, and soak a little longer if it still tastes salty.
Rinse the tomato, avocado and cilantro. Toss the lupini with the tomato, onion, garlic, oil, lime juice, pepper and salt, and let it sit for 10 minutes so the flavours mingle.

Fold in the diced avocado and cilantro and scatter the hemp hearts over the top just before eating. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Lupini are related to peanuts, so skip them if you have a peanut or lupin allergy. Eat only jarred or canned ready-to-eat lupini, never dry or raw lupin beans, and throw out any bean that tastes bitter.
recipes.tip: Peel the lupini skins off with your teeth, or eat them whole. No lupini? Use the same weight of rinsed canned white beans or chickpeas; the day will be lower in protein.

recipes.name: Lemon-cumin lupini dip with carrot and cucumber
recipes.about: Jarred lupini beans pulsed with lemon, garlic and cumin into a thick, chunky dip, with cucumber and carrot to scoop it up. It is a **very high-protein snack** that needs no cooking.

ingredients.note: jarred ready-to-eat lupini, soaked and rinsed

steps: Drain the lupini, cover them with fresh cold water and soak them in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, since the jar brine is very salty. Drain, rinse and taste one, and soak a little longer if it still tastes salty.

Rinse the cucumber and carrot. Pulse two thirds of the lupini in a food processor with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and a splash of cold water until thick and spreadable, or mash them with a fork. Stir in the rest of the whole lupini, the ground flax and the hemp hearts.

Serve the dip with the sliced cucumber and carrot sticks. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Lupini are related to peanuts, so skip them if you have a peanut or lupin allergy. Eat only jarred or canned ready-to-eat lupini, never dry or raw lupin beans, and throw out any bean that tastes bitter.
recipes.tip: Peel the lupini skins off first for a smoother dip, or leave them on for a chunkier one. No lupini? Use the same weight of rinsed canned white beans or chickpeas; the day will be lower in protein.

recipes.name: Maple-mustard roasted tempeh with carrot sticks
recipes.about: Little tempeh bites roasted in a sweet and tangy maple and mustard glaze, with crunchy carrot sticks for dipping. It is a **savoury soy protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C (410 °F). Steam the tempeh cubes over simmering water for 8 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the ground yellow mustard seed (dry mustard), maple syrup, soy sauce, lemon juice and oil. Toss the tempeh in the glaze and spread on a lined tray.
Roast for 15 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and sticky. Season with pepper.
Rinse, peel and cut the carrots and serve them with the warm tempeh.
recipes.tip: Make a double batch and keep it covered in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Cucumber-cilantro soy raita with spiced chickpeas and carrot sticks
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian cucumber raita
recipes.about: A cooling raita-style dip of soy yogurt and silken tofu with grated cucumber, cilantro and lemon, topped with warm, crisp cumin chickpeas and pumpkin seeds for crunch and served with carrot sticks for dipping. It makes a **creamy, savoury plant protein** snack.
steps: Rinse the chickpeas, drain them well and pat them dry. Warm the oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat, add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, until they smell nutty, then add the chickpeas and cook for 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until warm and crisp at the edges. Tip into a bowl.
Rinse the cucumber, cilantro and carrots. Grate the cucumber, squeeze out the water and mix it with the soy yogurt and silken tofu, whisked until smooth, with the cilantro, lemon juice and salt.

Top the raita with the warm chickpeas and the pumpkin seeds just before eating so they stay crunchy, and serve with the carrot sticks. Keep the raita covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Add a pinch of chaat masala or chili for more kick.

recipes.name: Chocolate peanut butter silken tofu pudding with raspberries
recipes.about: A thick, glossy chocolate pudding whipped from silken tofu, cocoa, peanut butter and maple syrup, spooned over raspberries and topped with pumpkin seeds for crunch. It is a **cool, high-protein snack** you can make the night before.
steps: Blend the silken tofu, cocoa, peanut butter, maple syrup and salt for 45 seconds, until completely smooth and thick, scraping down the sides once. Stir in the ground flax.
Rinse the raspberries and spoon them into a glass or bowl. Pour the pudding over and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Top with the pumpkin seeds just before eating. It keeps up to 2 days covered in the fridge. Once opened, keep tofu covered in the fridge and use it within 2 days.

recipes.name: Crispy cumin-roasted lupini with cucumber and carrot sticks
recipes.about: Jarred lupini beans roasted hot with cumin, chili and garlic until browned and crisp outside, then finished with lemon, ground flax and hemp hearts, with cool cucumber and carrot sticks alongside. It is a **crunchy, very high-protein snack** that bakes next to the tofu strips.

ingredients.note: jarred ready-to-eat lupini, soaked and rinsed

steps: Drain the lupini, cover them with fresh cold water and soak them in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight, since the jar brine is very salty. Drain, rinse and taste one, and soak a little longer if it still tastes salty.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Pat the lupini very dry with a clean towel, toss them with the oil, cumin, chili powder and salt, and spread them in one layer on a lined tray.

Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray twice and adding the garlic for the last 5 minutes, until browned and crisp outside. Squeeze over the lemon juice and toss with the ground flax and hemp hearts.

Rinse the cucumber and carrot, cut them in sticks and serve them alongside. The lupini are crunchiest warm and soften as they sit; keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Lupini are related to peanuts, so skip them if you have a peanut or lupin allergy. Eat only jarred or canned ready-to-eat lupini, never dry or raw lupin beans, and throw out any bean that tastes bitter.
recipes.tip: Roast them on the rack beside the ginger-soy tofu strips; both like 220 °C. Eat the skins or peel them with your teeth. No lupini? Use the same weight of rinsed canned chickpeas, roasted the same way; the day will be lower in protein.
